title: Store events carry no secret material
asA: operator who ships store event logs to a third-party observability provider
iWant: every field on every store event to be limited to store metadata; no domain data, no credential material, no secret values
soThat: a log-store breach is not a domain-data breach and the ops team does not have to negotiate a redaction rule with the provider

acceptanceCriteria.description: The fields on the facadeReady, migrationsApplied, backupExported, timeTravelRestored, and queryFailed events are restricted to store metadata: event name, ISO-8601 timestamp, binding name, environment name, database identifier, migration version integers and filenames, artifact paths, Time Travel bookmarks or timestamps, D1 error codes, and the domain-verb name that surfaced a queryFailed event. No event field carries a value read from a domain row.
acceptanceCriteria.given: the facade is exercised through open, one migrations-applied event on the ops surface, one export, one restore, and one deliberately failing query verb
acceptanceCriteria.when: every event record captured on the sink is inspected
acceptanceCriteria.then: every field on every record matches one of the metadata field types listed above, and no field's value equals a value read from any domain table

acceptanceCriteria.description: A grep of the facade source, the recovery runner source, and the deploy-gate hook source for domain-table column names and the values of well-known secret columns (session handles, token secrets, private keys, credential material) finds them referenced only inside the narrow CRUD verbs that read or write those columns, never inside event-emission call sites.
acceptanceCriteria.given: the facade source, the recovery runner source, and the deploy-gate hook source alongside the domain schema definition
acceptanceCriteria.then: matches appear only inside CRUD verb bodies (facade) or inside statements the recovery runner or deploy gate does not read for event-record construction, and never inside onEvent call arguments or event-record construction sites
